Adjusted read incorporating Beige Book insights:
- FOMC baseline remains: strong labor market, moderate growth, inflation below 2%, “soft” business fixed investment, and higher uncertainty; policy on hold with close monitoring, with one dissent favoring a cut.
- Beige Book cross-check (April to mid-May): activity expanded modestly across Districts; consumer spending improved and tourism was stronger in the Southeast; manufacturing and residential construction contributed but were mixed/modest; labor markets remained tight with notable shortages for lower-skill workers and only modest-to-moderate wage pressures; price pressures were modest; outlook generally positive but two-sided given trade and global risks.
- Credit tone: Beige Book suggests loan demand and conditions were generally steady-to-mixed, while the April SLOOS shows tighter C&I and construction/land-development standards and softer demand in several consumer categories. Together, these point to headwinds for capex and CRE, tempering the otherwise solid labor/consumption backdrop.

Net assessment: slightly positive growth outlook with increased two-sided risk; Beige Book modestly strengthens the growth side versus an SLOOS-only read but does not negate the investment/credit soft spots.
